clue.text: People like Sir Walter Raleigh — knight in ridiculously sizeable hat

indicators.note: in says the knight's letter is placed inside the scrambled letters around it
ridiculously says the letters of sizeable hat are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A picture of an Elizabethan courtier, knighted and sporting an absurdly large hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ridiculously' shuffles SIZEABLE HAT and 'in' places N among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Raleigh was a courtier of Queen Elizabeth I, so he and his contemporaries are Elizabethans.

clue.text: Ruler time and time again abandoning femme fatale

indicators.note: abandoning says the letters for time are dropped from the word for a femme fatale

parts.note: a femme fatale is a seductive temptress

indicators.note: and time again says the time letter is taken a second time

explanation.surface: A monarch repeatedly turning away a seductress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' removes both Ts, the first and the fifth letter, from TEMPTRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: An empress is a female sovereign, a ruler of an empire.

clue.text: Vexing one, pranksters at centre in capital city

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: in says the central letters go inside the name of the capital

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital

indicators.note: at centre picks the two middle letters of the word pranksters

explanation.surface: Someone annoying among a gang of practical jokers in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: With ten letters, PRANKSTERS has a two-letter centre rather than one.
explanation.definitionFit: Something irksome is irritating or annoying, which is what vexing describes.

clue.text: Giving tips for actors using gestures to communicate

indicators.note: tips for picks the two end letters of the word actors

parts.note: signing is communicating by gestures, as in sign language

explanation.surface: Advice for actors about using gestures to get a meaning across.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tips' looks like advice, but it means the ends of ACTORS: A and S.
explanation.definitionFit: To assign something is to allot or hand it over, so assigning is a synonym for giving.

clue.text: Docked 7 times

indicators.note: docked means cut short, so the final letter is removed from the word

parts.note: the answer to 7 Down is REMOVE, and erase means remove

explanation.surface: A terse note of how many times a ship docked.
explanation.walkthrough: The 7 points to 7 Down, REMOVE; a synonym, ERASE, loses its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Eras are periods or ages in history, which is one sense of times.

clue.text: Most robust force used in breaking the ties

indicators.note: used in says the letter for force is placed inside the other letters
breaking says the letters of the ties are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: The strongest force is needed to break the bonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' scrambles THE TIES and 'used in' puts F inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Hefty means big and strong, so the heftiest is the most robust.

clue.text: Famous piece of scripture incorporated in new edition

indicators.note: incorporated in says the scripture letters go inside the abbreviations

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a part of the Bible

explanation.surface: A well-known Bible passage included in a revised edition.
explanation.definitionFit: Noted means well known or celebrated, a straightforward synonym of famous.

clue.text: Withdraw from ramble around outside space

indicators.note: outside says the wandering word sits around the printer's space

parts.note: to rove is to ramble around, wander
an em is a printer's unit of space

explanation.surface: Pulling out of a country walk, going round outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: An EM is a typographic space the width of a letter M.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove is to take away or withdraw something, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Long time following stone steps

indicators.note: following says the long time comes after the stone abbreviation

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of 14 pounds
ages means a long time

explanation.surface: Stone steps that have been trodden for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone (ST) is a British weight of 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Stages are steps in a process or phases of progress.

clue.text: Spear fishes beside Welsh river

parts.note: pike are freshwater fish, so pikes are fishes
the Taff is the river flowing through Cardiff

explanation.surface: A fishing spear used beside a river in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: The Taff is the river running through Cardiff in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A pikestaff is the wooden shaft of a pike, the infantry weapon, so a kind of spear.

clue.text: Hazard scrubbing hot handle

indicators.note: scrubbing means cancelling or rubbing out, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a threat is a hazard or danger
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A warning about a hot handle that is dangerous to scrub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handle' looks like a noun, part of a pan, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat a person or thing is to deal with or manage it, a verb sense of handle.

clue.text: Plenty backing person that's unpleasant

indicators.note: backing says the word for a person is read backwards

parts.note: one means a person, as in someone
ugh is the exclamation said at something unpleasant

explanation.surface: Lots of support for a disagreeable individual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support but turns ONE into ENO.
explanation.definitionFit: Enough means as much as is needed, a sufficiency, close to plenty.

clue.text: Way lad breaks into grand musical sound

indicators.note: breaks into says the road and boy go inside the word for grand

parts.note: big means grand, large
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
a son is a boy, a lad

explanation.surface: A boy breaking into a grand house to the sound of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Birdsong is the tuneful calling of birds, a sound with musical quality.

clue.text: Interrupt idiots holding exercise class back

indicators.note: back says the whole assembled word is read in reverse
holding says the word for idiots contains the exercise class

parts.note: nits are idiots in British slang
PE is physical education, an exercise class at school

explanation.surface: Some fools are holding up the gym class, so someone must intervene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns round NIPETS, the whole assembly. Nit is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: To step in is to intervene in a situation, which is interrupting it.

clue.text: Runners from Spain with headwear covered in spots

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

indicators.note: covered in says the headwear is enclosed by the word for spots

parts.note: to spot something is to see it, so spots means sees
a cap is headwear

explanation.surface: Fugitives fleeing Spain wearing hats and covered in spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spots' looks like a rash but is the verb, to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Escapees are people who have run away from captivity, so runners in the sense of fugitives.

clue.text: Read a pulp novel; one that's cheering

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of read a pulp are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An instruction to read cheap pulp fiction, followed by someone cheering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book, fitting pulp fiction, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An applauder claps or cheers in approval, someone who is cheering.

clue.text: Junk aircraft model set up and working

parts.note: a jet is an aircraft

indicators.note: set up, in a down clue, says the word for model is written upwards, in reverse

parts.note: to sit for an artist is to model
on means working, functioning

explanation.surface: A model plane is thrown out but then rebuilt and running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Junk' looks like a noun (or a Chinese ship) but is the verb, to throw away.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to throw away or discard, which is junking something.

clue.text: Struggles of girl disheartened having entered wrong answer

indicators.note: having entered says the shortened girl goes inside the scrambled letters
wrong says the letters of answer are put out of order
disheartened means losing the heart, so only the outer letters of girl remain

explanation.surface: A dejected girl giving a wrong answer has a hard time of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' removes IR, the heart of the word; 'wrong' scrambles to WRANES, and 'having entered' places the remnant after its fourth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrangles are long disputes or quarrels, a sense of struggles.

clue.text: At same time as card game, hosting introduction to ludo

indicators.note: hosting says the card game contains the next letter

parts.note: whist is a card game for four players

indicators.note: introduction to picks the first letter of the word ludo

explanation.surface: Playing cards while also starting a board game.
explanation.definitionFit: Whilst is a conjunction meaning while, during the time that something else happens.

clue.text: Emerged from parish, Kent, where all outsiders are ignored

indicators.note: ignoring all outsiders drops the first and last letters of each word, keeping the insides

explanation.surface: Something that came out of a Kent parish that shuns strangers.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England. PARISH without P and H gives ARIS; KENT without K and T gives EN.
explanation.definitionFit: Arisen means come up or come into being, a past participle matching emerged.

clue.text: Did without resort wine

parts.note: a spa is a health resort
red is red wine

explanation.surface: Someone at a resort who went without wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To spare something can mean to manage without it, to forgo it, as in 'can you spare it?'.

clue.text: Ulcers troubled English hermit

indicators.note: troubled says the letters of ulcers are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A hermit suffering from painful ulcers.
explanation.definitionFit: A recluse lives alone apart from society, just as a hermit does.

clue.text: Abandons desires to have Democrat leading

indicators.note: leading says the Democrat letter goes in front

parts.note: itches are cravings, desires

explanation.surface: A politician gives up his ambitions so a Democrat can lead.
explanation.definitionFit: To ditch something is to get rid of or drop it, so ditches means abandons.

clue.text: Lack of fairness some strain, I quit yesterday

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone describing an injustice: the stress got too much and they walked out yesterday.
explanation.definitionFit: Iniquity is gross injustice or wickedness, the absence of fair dealing.

clue.text: Part of drainage system not good state

indicators.note: not says the good letter is left out of the drainage word

parts.note: a gutter carries rainwater off a roof or road

explanation.surface: A report that part of the drains is in a poor condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like a noun, condition, but it is the verb, to say.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter is to say or express aloud, which is to state.

clue.text: Good-luck charm mother's put by bed

parts.note: ma is mother, so mother's gives MA'S
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A mother leaves a lucky charm by the bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a person, animal or object thought to bring good fortune.

clue.text: Very loudly going after game bird

indicators.note: going after says the musical letters follow the game

parts.note: RU is rugby union
ff, fortissimo, is the musical direction for very loud

explanation.surface: Someone chasing game birds very noisily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game bird' reads as one phrase but splits: game is RU, bird is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The ruff is a wading bird whose males grow showy neck feathers.

clue.text: Lovely set of furniture picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word for the furniture set is taken by its sound

parts.note: a suite is a matching set of furniture

explanation.surface: A charming furniture set someone has bought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' looks like collecting the furniture, but it signals hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet means pleasant or charming, an informal synonym for lovely.

clue.text: Start to save our money for bread

indicators.note: start to picks the first letter of the word save

parts.note: dough is slang for money

explanation.surface: Advice to begin saving our cash for food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bread' is also slang for money, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Sourdough is bread leavened with a fermented starter.

clue.text: Sausages free — oddly rotten encased in hairy skins

parts.note: frank means open, free in speech

indicators.note: encased in says the odd letters go inside the word for hairy skins

parts.note: furs are animal pelts, hairy skins

indicators.note: oddly picks the first, third and fifth letters of the word rotten

explanation.surface: Free sausages, but strangely rotten and wrapped in hairy casings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like 'strangely' but takes RTE from ROTTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Frankfurters are smoked sausages named after Frankfurt.
